channel.title: Jeep recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer Roof Rack Crossbars May Come Loose
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer, and Grand Wagoneer L vehicles because the pivot bolts holding the roof rack crossbars may not have been tightened correctly. This could let the crossbars come loose and detach from the roof while the vehicle is being driven, rather than staying securely attached as intended.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Rear Coil Spring May Detach
item.description: On these Jeep Grand Cherokee models, the rear coil springs may have been installed incorrectly. Because of this, a spring can come loose and separate from the vehicle while you are driving. This recall replaces two earlier recalls for the same problem, and vehicles already repaired under those earlier recalls will still need this new fix.

item.title: Jeep tire pressure warning system may miss low tires
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Cherokee 4xe, Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer and Cherokee vehicles. A software error means the tire pressure monitoring system may not detect a tire that is low, or may not turn on the tire pressure warning light the way it should. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal standard for tire pressure monitoring systems. Dealers will update the software free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer gear display may not appear
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Wagoneer and Wagoneer L vehicles. A software error can keep the display that shows which gear the transmission is in from appearing at all. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard that covers the shift lever sequence, the starter interlock and the transmission braking effect. Dealers will update the software in the shifter module.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator Steering Pump Fire Risk
item.description: Certain Jeep Wrangler, Wrangler 4xe, and Gladiator vehicles have an electric hydraulic power steering pump with wiring that can overheat. This overheating can cause a vehicle fire, and this can happen even when the vehicle is parked with the ignition off.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Side Air Bags May Deploy Late
item.description: A software error in the computer that controls the air bags may cause the side air bags to deploy late during a crash, instead of deploying when needed. This affects certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. Dealers will fix the problem by updating the control module's software, free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee Power Transfer Unit May Fail
item.description: Some Jeep Cherokee vehicles have a power transfer unit that may fail. If it fails, the vehicle could lose the power that drives the wheels, or the vehicle could roll away on its own.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S and Dodge Charger EV display may fail
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer S and Dodge Charger electric vehicles. A software problem can make the display in front of the driver stop working, so the information it normally shows is not available. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet several federal safety standards, covering vehicle lamps, stability control, brakes, the tire pressure monitoring system and occupant crash protection.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S Liftgate Hinge Cover May Detach
item.description: The liftgate is the hatch at the back of the vehicle, and the cover over its hinge is meant to clip into place. On the vehicles being recalled, that hinge cover may not have been clipped in properly and can come off the vehicle. Dealers will inspect the cover and will repair or replace it if it is not secured the way it should be.

item.title: Jeep And Ram Trailer Tow Module Failure
item.description: On these Jeep Wagoneer S, Ram, and Jeep Cherokee vehicles, the trailer tow module was not designed correctly. Because of this, the lights on a trailer you're towing may fail to come on, and the trailer's brakes may not work.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Rear Coil Springs Can Detach
item.description: On certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles, the rear coil springs may not have been installed the right way. Because of this, a spring could work loose and detach from the vehicle while you are driving it. Jeep already mailed owners a letter warning about this risk, and will send a second letter once the final repair is ready, expected in March 2026.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee 4XE Engine Can Fail From Debris
item.description: Some of these hybrid engines were built with debris left inside them. That debris can cause the engine to fail. If the engine fails, the vehicle can suddenly lose drive power while you are driving. An engine failure can also lead to a fire starting in the engine compartment. Both a sudden loss of power and an engine fire put people in and around the vehicle at greater risk.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler, Grand Cherokee Battery Fire Risk
item.description: These Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe vehicles have a high voltage battery that may fail internally. This failure can lead to a vehicle fire, whether the vehicle is parked or being driven. A vehicle fire increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer Window Trim Piece Can Detach
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer SUVs. A trim piece next to the driver's and passenger's front windows, called the quarter trim, may not have been properly secured when the vehicle was built. Because it was not attached the correct way, this trim piece can come loose and detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer door trim may come off the vehicle
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer and Jeep Grand Wagoneer vehicles. The trim on the driver and passenger doors may not have been installed properly when the vehicles were built, and that can allow the trim to come off the vehicle. Dealers will inspect the door trim and replace it if needed, at no cost to the owner. Owner notification letters about this recall were mailed on September 25, 2025.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S Recalled for Wrong Cross Beam
item.description: These Jeep Wagoneer S vehicles have the wrong support beam installed behind the dashboard. This beam is supposed to help protect people inside the vehicle if it's ever in a crash, but because the wrong one was used, it doesn't meet federal crash-protection standards. That means it may not do its job properly to protect occupants if a collision happens.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV, Jeep Wagoneer S May Roll Away
item.description: On these Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S electric vehicles, an incorrectly installed spring may cause the vehicle to lose its 'Park' function when the gear selector is placed in Park, which can lead to the vehicle rolling away.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee PHEV May Lose Drive Power
item.description: On these Jeep Grand Cherokee plug-in hybrid vehicles, a software error in the hybrid control processor may cause the vehicle to lose drive power.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Head Restraints May Not Lock
item.description: Chrysler says the head restraints on the second-row seats in some Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles may not lock into the upright position. Because these head restraints can fail to lock, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety requirement covering head restraints. Owners are being notified so the head restraints can be checked and fixed if needed.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee blower motor may fail, disabling defroster
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. The blower motor, the fan that pushes air through the vents, can fail. If it fails, the system that clears fog and frost from the windshield stops working. Federal safety rules set requirements for windshield defrosting and defogging, and these vehicles do not meet them. A dealer will inspect the blower motor and replace it if needed, at no cost.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee Drivetrain Failure Can Cause Rollaway
item.description: The part that sends engine power to the wheels can become damaged and disconnect the transmission and differential. This can cause the vehicle to lose drive power, or lose the ability to stay in park. Dealers will update the drivetrain control module and the power transfer unit's software, and replace the unit if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S Headlights May Not Aim Correctly
item.description: Chrysler says the headlights on certain Jeep Wagoneer S electric vehicles cannot be properly adjusted. The part used to adjust the headlights up and down is not accessible, and the part covering the side-to-side adjustment is not covered the way it should be. Because of this, the headlights may not be aimed correctly.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee rearview camera may go blank
item.description: This recall affects certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. A part inside the center touchscreen display may overheat. If that happens, the rearview camera image may not display on the screen.

item.title: Jeep SUVs: Rearview Camera Image May Not Show
item.description: Chrysler (FCA) is recalling certain 2024 Jeep Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer, Grand Cherokee, and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. Incorrect software in the rearview camera module may cause the rearview camera image to not display when the driver puts the vehicle in reverse. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet federal rear visibility requirements.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Radiator Crossmember Bolts May Be Loose
item.description: On certain 2024 Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles, the bolts that secure the radiator crossmember may not be properly secured. If the crossmember is not secure, it can lead to improper air bag deployment and a fuel leak during a crash.

item.title: Jeep Renegade Recalled for Wrong Reverse Lights
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Renegade vehicles because the wrong reverse light assembly was installed on the rear bumper. These incorrect lights may not work as intended, which can reduce how well other drivers and pedestrians see that the vehicle is backing up. This means people nearby may not get a clear signal that the vehicle is in reverse, making it harder for them to notice it is backing up.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Side Air Bag Connector May Fail
item.description: A connector for the front seat side air bags may not have been properly secured, which could prevent the air bags from deploying. This affects certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. Dealers have already secured the connector on all affected vehicles, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Speedometer Software Display Error
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles. These vehicles have a software error in the instrument panel cluster. Because of this error, the speedometer may show the wrong vehicle speed instead of the actual speed the vehicle is traveling. This means the vehicle does not meet a federal safety standard that covers how vehicle displays and controls must work.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Durango Brake Module Fault
item.description: In some Grand Cherokee and Durango SUVs, a malfunction in the antilock brake module can incorrectly turn on the brake lights and disable the antilock brakes and stability control. It may also allow the vehicle to be started and shifted out of Park without the driver pressing the brake pedal.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee 4xe High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: The high voltage battery in these vehicles may fail internally. If this internal battery failure happens, it can lead to a vehicle fire. This can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven at the time of the failure.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler Camera and Brake Light Failure
item.description: On these Jeep Wrangler vehicles, the wiring for the rearview camera and the center brake light can short circuit. If that happens, the rearview camera image may stop showing, and the center brake light may stop working, so it no longer lights up when the driver brakes.

item.title: Jeep Gladiator, Wrangler: Instrument Panel Cluster May Fail
item.description: The instrument panel cluster on affected vehicles may develop an internal short circuit and stop working.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee L child seat tether welds weak
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain 2024 Jeep Grand Cherokee L vehicles. The welds that hold the child seat tether anchors on the second row seat back frame may not be strong enough. If the welds are insufficient, the seat may not be able to hold a child's car seat in place properly during a crash. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal standard for child restraint anchorage systems. Dealers will reinforce the welds free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator Software May Stall Engine
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain 2021 Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator vehicles that were already repaired once under an earlier recall. The software that controls the powertrain may cause the engine to stall, which can take away the vehicle's ability to keep driving under its own power. This recall provides an updated software fix for vehicles that still need it, including ones that received the previous repair.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee Side Airbag Connector Not Secured
item.description: In certain Jeep Cherokee vehicles, the connector for the right-side curtain airbag may not be properly secured. This could keep the airbag from deploying the way it's supposed to.

item.title: Jeep Renegade front airbag may not deploy as intended
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Renegade vehicles, along with some Alfa Romeo and Fiat models. A sensor switch in a front seat belt buckle may not be connected properly, and because of that the front seat airbag may not inflate the way it is meant to. Dealers will repair the connection, and owner notification letters were mailed beginning in late August 2024.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Second-Row Seat Belt Bolt Loose
item.description: In some Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles, the bolt that holds the second-row seat belt buckle in place may not have been tightened properly. Because the buckle is not securely anchored, the seat belt may not hold an occupant in place the way it should during a crash. This can reduce how well the seat belt protects a person sitting in the second row, increasing the risk of injury if a crash occurs.

item.title: Chrysler, Jeep, Ram Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: A software issue in the radio can prevent the rearview camera image from displaying on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the requirements of the federal safety standard for rear visibility, FMVSS 111. To fix the problem, dealers will update the radio software, or the software update will be delivered over-the-air. This repair is free of charge for owners of the affected vehicles.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Missing Foam May Affect Airbags
item.description: The front bumper on affected vehicles may be missing energy-absorbing foam. Without this foam in place, the front air bags may not deploy the way they are designed to.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain 2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L vehicles because the screen module connections were not fastened properly. This can stop the rearview camera image from appearing on the display when the vehicle is shifted into reverse. A rearview image that does not display gives the driver less visibility, which can increase the risk of a crash.
